Name: Base blocks
What it means: How many blocks a map starts with. Fixed forever once the map is created
Formula: Chosen at creation; default defaultBaseBlocks

Name: Level
What it means: A map's difficulty, 1 to 10. Each map has its own
Formula: L = 1 + floor(log2(mined / E + 1)), at most maxLevel

Name: Blocks mined
What it means: Every new block first claimed on that map, by players and factories
Formula: Counts up by 1 per first claim

Name: Level start
What it means: Blocks mined on a map when level L begins

Name: Terrain factor
What it means: How hard the terrain is: sand 0.5, grass 1, forest 1.5, stone 3, gold 1. Water can't be claimed

Name: Hardness
What it means: Hits to mine a block. A block keeps the level it was born at
Formula: H = hitsPerBlock x 2^(L-1) x t

Name: Click Power
What it means: Hits each tap counts as
Formula: Tier value

Name: Defense
What it means: Multiplies the hits others need to take your block
Formula: Hits to take = H x D (+ walls)

Name: Pay
What it means: Squares for mining a new block. Taking an owned block pays nothing
Formula: S = H / hitsPerSquare x M_earn + G

Name: Earnings
What it means: Multiplies pay
Formula: Tier value

Name: Gold bonus
What it means: Extra squares for first claiming a gold block

Name: Work-hour
What it means: One hour of base mining. The unit every price is measured in
Formula: 1 Wh at level L = W(L) squares

Name: Work index
What it means: Squares one work-hour is worth at level L
Formula: W(L) = (3600 / baseBlockSeconds) x 2^(L-1) = 1,200 x 2^(L-1)

Name: Payback hours
What it means: How long an object takes to repay its price

Name: Value per hour
What it means: Work-hours an object gives (or forces an attacker to spend) per hour

Name: Universal price
What it means: The price of anything with a V
Formula: Price = P x V x W(L)

Name: Tier
What it means: Upgrade tier, 1 to 10. Tier 1 is open from the start; each tier is bought in S small steps
Where the number lives: Each player; Upgrades tab Steps per tier

Name: Tier range
What it means: What an upgrade gives at the start and the end of tier N. Every tier max is the last one times the multiplier
Formula: lo_1 = Tier 1 start; lo_N = Tier 1 max x m^(N-2); hi_N = Tier 1 max x m^(N-1)

Name: Value after step s
What it means: Big gains on the first steps, flattening toward the tier max
Formula: lo_N + (hi_N - lo_N) x ln(1 + g x s / S) / ln(1 + g)

Name: Price of step s
What it means: Cheap at first, then rising and flattening toward the end of the tier
Formula: T x W(N) x ln(1 + c x s / S) / sum of ln(1 + c x j / S) for j = 1 to S

Name: Tier cost
What it means: Work-hours to buy all of one tier's steps, priced at that tier's level
Formula: T x W(N) squares

Name: Tier in use
What it means: Your upgrades work at most up to the level of the block you act on
Formula: min(your tier, the block's level)

Name: Factory price
What it means: Price of your nth factory
Formula: P_F x V_F x W(L) x g^(n-1)

Name: Factory hits
What it means: Hits a factory adds per second
Formula: (hitsPerBlock / baseBlockSeconds) x Factory Speed value

Name: Factory distance
What it means: Extra hits when a factory's target lies outside its home square (d = blocks outside it)
Formula: d x factoryDistancePenaltyWh x W(L) x hitsPerSquare

Name: Wall strength
What it means: Hits to break a wall
Formula: w x H

Name: Wall price
What it means: Price of one wall; the same for every wall in a batch
Formula: wallPriceWh x W(L of the block) x max(1, sqrt(walls you own on this map) / 2)

Name: Skin price
What it means: Price of a skin
Formula: rarity hours x W(L)

Name: Market fee
What it means: Share of each land sale destroyed
Formula: price x marketFee
